newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt prices end up, Venezuela outperforms.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt prices end up, Venezuela outperforms.

text.p: Emerging debt prices wound down the New York trading session on a positive note with Venezuela strongly outperforming others, traders said.
"We saw Bradys have a good day all around, but the outperformer today was Venezuela," said Pablo Goldberg, Latin American economist at I.D.E.A. Inc.
Venezuela PARs traded up 1-3/8 to 73-1/2 bid and Venezuela FLIRBs were up 1-1/4 to 88-3/8 bid, traders said.
"We had strong comments from Venezuela coming out of the meetings in Barcelona," said one Brady trader. "Venezuela was the key gainer in today's session."
On Tuesday, finance minister Luis Raul Matos Axocar said Venezuela was aiming to make a decision on a plan to smooth out repayments on outstanding commercial debt by the middle of next month.

Under current terms, Venezuela would have to pay $3 billion, or 40 percent of ordinary income, every year through 1999 to service its outstanding debt. Matos said Venezuela was aiming to reduce this to 25 percent.

Players also cited recent news that the Venezuelan governement, union and private sector leaders had signed a historic agreement to reform the country's severance payment system, opening the way for a wider reform of the country's decaying social security system.
The agreement which still has to be passed by Congress would mark the beginning of the freeing-up of Venezuela's rigid labor markets.
"This historical agreement involving these reforms was very positive news," said I.D.E.A.'s Goldberg.
Meanwhile, players said Bradys traded up today on better buying activity and a more supportive U.S. Treasury market.
"We saw some client buying late yesterday and some more today...generally the market gained good support from the Treasury market," another Brady trader said.
The benchmark U.S. Treasury bond ended off 2/32 at 95-25/32 to yield 6.96 percent at the close.
Bradys erased Monday's losses with spreads seen tighter by about 15 to 20 basis points, traders said.
"What characterized today's market was that it was dealer driven and generally better bid," the trader added.
Among key gainers on Tuesday was Argentina, Par bonds were up 1/8 at 64-3/4 bid, FRBs ended 3/4 higher at 90-1/8 bid.
Boosting Argentina's debt was Tuesday's comments by Economy minister Roque Fernandez that Argentina would repay earlier $750 million of its Paris Club debt.
Argentina hopes to reach an agreement with the IMF on an extended fund facility to replace the stand-by loan programme it has had since 1995.
"We're going to pay back in advance $750 million to the Paris Club within our 1997 budget," Fernandez told Reuters during the annual meeting of the Inter-American Development Bank.
Turning to other Brady bonds, Mexico Pars were up 3/8 at 72-7/8 bid and Discounts were up 3/4 at 88-7/8 bid. Brazil C were up 3/8 to 76-5/8 bid.
Bulgaria FLRB were up 1/8 at 45-1/8 bid, IABs also traded up 1/8 at 60-1/8 bid, traders said.
Russian VN US$ traded up 1/4 to end the New York trading session at 81-3/4 bid.

Meanwhile, market participants continue to cast a watchful eye on the Federal Open Market Committee, the policy-setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board, which is set to meet next week to vote on U.S. monetary policy.
(( -- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
